chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who fasted, then presumed that the sun had set while there was cloud cover in the sky, so he broke his fast, and then the clouds cleared and the sun had not set. He said: 'His fast is complete and he does not have to make it up.'

key_terms.لاَ يَقْضِيهِ: he does not make it up

ai.seo_question: Does a fast break if I eat because I thought the sun set due to clouds, but it was still there?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the principle of 'presumption of correctness' (al-zann al-mu'tamad) in fasting, ruling that a valid fast is not invalidated by an honest mistake regarding sunset visibility. It highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on ease and the removal of hardship (raf' al-haraj), ensuring that believers are not penalized for reasonable errors in natural observation. This ruling is foundational in distinguishing between intentional breaking of the fast and unintentional error due to environmental factors like cloud cover.
